cleanIntro: SIG's Classic Line strip as it applies to the P220 — hammer-fired, takedown lever to six o'clock, slide off the front. One book covers seven Classic Line pistols, and the P220 is the one it treats differently: it is the only model offered with the single-action-only trigger and its thumb safety, which has its own appendix. The Elite pistols with the Short Reset Trigger have a changed strip of their own. Both are settled in the first step.

steps.title: Find out which P220 you have before you strip it
steps.action: Establish your P220's trigger system and whether it has the Short Reset Trigger. A P220 SAO is single action only and carries a thumb safety on the frame, above and to the rear of the grip; a DA/SA P220 has a decocking lever; DAK and DAO pistols have neither. An Elite Series pistol with the SRT has a different slide-removal sequence. If you are unsure about the SRT, treat the pistol as SRT and use the fork step later in this guide.
steps.prose: This is the one Classic Line book where the answer changes your procedure. The SAO pistol has a manual safety the others lack, and SIG's SAO appendix puts it first in the unloading sequence. The SRT pistol needs to be decocked as the slide closes or its safety lever will not retract far enough for the slide to come off the frame.
steps.aside: SIG's book keeps separate parts diagrams for the P220 DA/SA/DAK and the P220 SAO (sections 12.0 and 12.1).
steps.quote: A fourth system, single action only (SAO) is available in the P220 only.

steps.title: What this manual covers — and the strip it does not cover
steps.action: Understand the scope of the book these steps come from before you rely on it. This manual covers seven Classic Line pistols together — P220, P224, P225, P226, P227, P229 and P239 — and bounds itself twice in ways that matter to a P220 owner. The single-action-only procedures in its Appendix B are for the P220 SAO only. And its standard disassembly does not cover SRT-equipped pistols: SIG carves their slide removal out into Appendix C, with its own steps.
steps.prose: Neither is bookkeeping. Following the standard steps on an SRT pistol means forcing a slide against a safety lever that has not retracted, and the SAO steps describe a thumb safety that a DA/SA, DAK or DAO P220 does not have. Where a procedure in the source manual carries a model qualifier, that qualifier is the instruction.
steps.quote: Note: Steps 5 and 6 below are not applicable to SRT (Short Reset Trigger) models.  See Appendix C.

steps.warn: A procedure printed next to yours in a multi-model manual is not automatically yours. Check the heading it sits under.

steps.title: P220 SAO only: thumb safety up before you unload
steps.action: On a P220 SAO, push the thumb safety fully upward to engage it before you do anything else; the white dot on the safety shows when it is on. The safety does not lock the slide, so you can unload with it engaged. On a DA/SA, DAK or DAO P220, skip this step.
steps.prose: SIG's single-action pistol stays cocked after every shot, and the thumb safety is what blocks the hammer while your hands are on the slide and the magazine catch. It can only be put on with the slide fully closed, so engage it before you lock the slide back, not after.
steps.quote: Always engage the thumb safety before loading and unloading the pistol.

steps.warn: The thumb safety cannot be engaged with the slide open. Put it on first, while the slide is closed.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Depress the magazine catch behind the trigger guard and draw the magazine out of the frame, then move it away from the bench.
steps.prose: Dropping the magazine does nothing to a round already in the chamber, which is why SIG writes unloading as two separate jobs: the magazine first, then the chamber.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine catch and remove the magazine.

steps.title: Eject the chambered round and lock the slide open
steps.action: Pull the slide back to its stop and engage the slide catch lever so the slide stays open. Any chambered round is ejected as you do it — watch it go and find it on the bench.
steps.prose: Do this whether or not you think the chamber is empty. The hammer's position tells you nothing about the chamber on any P220 trigger system.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to the stop and engage the slide catch lever. The round is ejected and the slide is locked open.

steps.title: Check the chamber by eye and by hand
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the ejection port and down the magazine well, then put a finger into the chamber mouth.
steps.prose: SIG asks for a manual check as well as a visual one. A case in shadow at the rear of the chamber is easy to read as bare metal; a finger does not make that mistake.
steps.quote: Visually and manually check the chamber to ensure the pistol is completely free of ammunition.

steps.title: Slide locked open, chamber confirmed empty again
steps.action: With the pistol unloaded, retract the slide to its stop and lock it open on the slide catch lever, then confirm once more — visually and physically — that there is no round in the chamber.
steps.prose: SIG builds a second chamber check into the disassembly procedure itself rather than relying on the one you did while unloading. Do it as a fresh check, not as a formality.
steps.quote: Verify visually and physically that there is no round in the chamber.

steps.title: Takedown lever clockwise to six o'clock
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever above the trigger, on the left side of the frame, clockwise until it points straight down at six o'clock.
steps.prose: Six o'clock is a definite position, not an approximate one. If the lever will not rotate, the slide is not locked fully back.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise to a vertical (6 o’clock) position.

steps.title: SRT models fork here
steps.action: If your P220 has the Short Reset Trigger, stop following the standard sequence now and use SIG's supplemental steps: pull the slide back slightly to disengage the slide catch lever, hold it firmly and let it move forward slowly, and as the slide reaches its closed position decock the pistol. Then slip the whole assembly forward off the frame. If your pistol is not SRT, continue with the next step instead.
steps.prose: The decocking is the whole point of the fork: it lets the SRT safety lever retract completely so the slide can clear the frame. Skipping it leaves the slide hard against that lever, and pulling harder is what damages it.
steps.quote: As the slide reaches its closed position, decock the pistol. This will allow the SRT safety lever to completely retract so the slide can be fully removed from the frame.

steps.title: Non-SRT: release the catch and let the slide run forward under control
steps.action: On a P220 without the SRT, pull the slide back slightly to disengage the slide catch lever, then let it travel forward in a controlled fashion. Keep a hand on it the whole way.
steps.prose: Controlled means your hand slows it, not the frame. Once the catch lever is down the slide is held by nothing but the recoil spring's tension and your grip, and the spring wants it forward.
steps.caution: Eye protection on. The slide is under spring tension; keep positive control of it.
steps.quote: Retract the slide slightly to disengage the slide catch lever. Allow the slide to move forward in a controlled fashion.

steps.title: Slide assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the complete slide assembly — slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide together — straight forward off the frame rails.
steps.prose: It leaves as one unit. Keep it square to the frame as it comes off, and keep a hand under it: the recoil spring and guide are not firmly attached to the slide.
steps.quote: Move the complete slide assembly (slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide) forward and off the frame.

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down, push the recoil spring guide forward slightly to unseat it, then lift it out from the rear.
steps.prose: Forward, then lift from the rear. SIG warns that the spring and guide are under tension and not firmly attached to the slide, so hold them as they unseat.
steps.caution: Eye protection on. Keep the muzzle end of the slide pointed away from your face while the guide unseats.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring guide forward slightly and lift from rear to remove the recoil spring and guide from the slide.

steps.action: Lift the barrel slightly and draw it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Up a fraction, then straight back. If it will not move, the recoil spring guide is still in the slide.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling upward slightly and to the rear.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four pieces: slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide, and the frame. That is the whole of SIG's owner-level P220 strip, on every trigger system.
steps.prose: Nothing past this is an owner job in this manual — the hammer, sear, decocking or safety parts and the extractor all stay where they are. The book keeps P220 parts diagrams for the DA/SA/DAK and SAO pistols if you need to identify a component without taking anything further apart.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to allow a thorough cleaning after shooting.

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off — the spring is compressed
deepSteps.action: Empty the magazine. Find the bottom of the floorplate, then with a punch or cleaning rod depress the magazine insert through it and push the floorplate forward until it is clear of the tube. Keep a thumb over the insert as it releases.
deepSteps.prose: The insert is holding a compressed spring, and SIG's instruction is explicitly to guard the insert and spring with your thumb. Depress just far enough to clear, and slide the floorplate — do not lever it off.
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch, cleaning rod, or similar tool, depress the magazine insert and push the magazine floorplate forward until it is clear of the magazine tube.

deepSteps.title: Follower and spring out
deepSteps.action: Draw the follower and spring out of the tube, noting which way the follower sits on the spring before it clears.
deepSteps.prose: SIG's reassembly asks for the follower to be correctly positioned on the spring, so note it now. This is as far as the magazine goes for cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the magazine follower and magazine spring from the magazine tube. This level of disassembly is sufficient to allow a thorough cleaning after shooting.

deepSteps.title: Bore brush in from the chamber end
deepSteps.action: With the barrel out of the slide, oil the cleaning brush and enter the bore from the chamber end — never from the muzzle. Push it through and out.
deepSteps.prose: Entering from the chamber keeps the rod off the muzzle. Use a suitable rod and a brush of the correct caliber, and never a steel wire brush.
deepSteps.quote: Lubricate the cleaning brush with gun oil and insert it into the barrel via the chamber (opposite the muzzle end).

deepSteps.title: Patch the bore and chamber
deepSteps.action: Push cleaning patches through the bore and chamber until they come out clean of powder residue and oil.
deepSteps.prose: Patches after the brush, not instead of it — the brush breaks the fouling loose and the patches carry it out. Keep going until a patch comes out clean rather than to a fixed count.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe powder residues and oil from the barrel bore and chamber with cleaning patches.

deepSteps.title: Frame guides, slide interior and the recoil assembly
deepSteps.action: Work a brush or cleaning patch over the frame guides, the inside and outside of the slide, and the recoil spring and its guide, then lightly lubricate the same surfaces with an oiled cloth.
deepSteps.prose: These are the surfaces the slide runs on. Light is the standard — SIG cautions against over-lubrication twice on the same page.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Oiled brush of the correct caliber, entered from the chamber end only
Never a steel wire brush — it damages the bore surface
Patches through until they come out clean
Brush the exterior of the barrel with an oiled brush
Light oil in bore and chamber, then wipe the excess back out

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Brush or patch the frame guides and the inside and outside of the slide
Light film of gun oil or gun grease on the same surfaces, applied with a cloth
All-stainless pistols such as the P220 ST take a lubricant designed for stainless steel
Do not over-lubricate — SIG cautions against it by name

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING AND GUIDE
tasks: Brush or patch the spring and the guide clean
Check the spring for kinks and the guide for bends while it is out

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the tube inside and out and the follower
Check the follower moves freely down the full length of the tube
Check the tube's condition and that the floorplate locks back on securely

reassembly: Verify the pistol is clear of all foreign matter, then insert the barrel into the slide.
Insert the recoil spring guide assembly into the slide — it is under spring tension and is not firmly attached, so keep control of it.
Make sure the takedown lever is rotated clockwise to the vertical six o'clock position.
Guide the slide onto the frame rails from the front, retract it fully to the rear, and engage the slide catch lever to lock it open.
Rotate the takedown lever counter-clockwise until horizontal, then depress the slide catch lever to release the slide.

DA/SA pistols: decock the hammer with the decocking lever. SIG notes this step is not applicable to DAO or DAK pistols. A P220 SAO has no decocking lever in SIG's description; its appendix ends unloading by releasing the thumb safety and squeezing the trigger with the muzzle in a safe direction, and warns never to ease the hammer down by hand.
fncheck: Magazine out and the pistol confirmed unloaded, muzzle in a safe direction. Check the recoil spring and slide travel: retract the slide fully and release it, verify it locks fully in the closed position, and repeat. On a DA/SA, DAK or DAO P220, check the trigger mechanism: pull the trigger fully to the rear and watch the hammer cock as the trigger travels back; at the end of travel the hammer should fall forward firmly. SIG's book describes that trigger check only; on a P220 SAO the hammer is cocked by the slide, and the book prints no separate SAO trigger check. Then check the slide catch lever: insert an empty magazine, retract the slide fully and release it, verify the slide locks to the rear, depress the slide catch lever and verify the slide closes; remove the magazine. Inspect the magazine and the pistol's exterior, sights and takedown lever. Never use a pistol or magazine that is damaged or fails a function check — SIG asks for it to be returned to SIG SAUER for evaluation.
